title: Hameroff's view of microtubules and anesthesia as the switch for consciousness

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes the idea of an anesthesiologist named Stuart Hameroff, who worked with the physicist Roger Penrose, author of the book The Emperor's New Mind. Microtubules are tiny tube-shaped structures inside our cells, and Michels says Hameroff found that when anesthesia shuts them off, the rest of the brain and body keep working normally but the person loses consciousness. If true, it would mean these tiny structures are the switch for consciousness itself.
